pairs.locus: Pico della Mirandola, Oratio de Hominis Dignitate 47-48
pairs.question: Quorsum haec?
pairs.answer: Ut intelligamus, postquam hac nati sumus conditione, ut id simus quod esse volumus, curare hoc potissimum debere nos, ut illud quidem in nos non dicatur, cum in honore essemus non cognovisse similes factos brutis et iumentis insipientibus.
pairs.derivation: The author asks to what end all the foregoing tends and answers it himself. Dropped the framing connective 'Sed' from the head of the question and normalized capitalization. The answer is the single sentence (48) that directly gives the purpose ('Ut intelligamus...'), ending at the first full stop ('...iumentis insipientibus'); what follows (49, 'Sed illud potius Asaph prophetae...') turns to a further exhortation and is not part of the direct answer.

pairs.locus: Pico della Mirandola, Oratio de Hominis Dignitate 79-80
pairs.question: Quis Domini scalas vel sordidato pede, vel male mundis manibus attinget?
pairs.answer: Impuro, ut habent mysteria, purum attingere nephas.
pairs.derivation: The author poses an interrogative ('who will touch the Lord's ladder with dirty foot or unclean hands?') and answers it. Quoted the self-contained interrogative clause of sentence 79; omitted the preceding conditional preamble ('Quod si hoc idem nobis angelicam affectantibus vitam factitandum est, queso,') which is framing/setup and not part of the utterance, and normalized 'quis' to 'Quis'. The answer is the whole of sentence 80 ('it is forbidden for the impure to touch the pure'), which directly answers; the next sentences (81-82, 'Sed qui hi pedes? Quae manus?') open a new line of questioning.

pairs.locus: Pico della Mirandola, Oratio de Hominis Dignitate 223 (Plato, Epinomis)
pairs.question: Cur homo animal sapientissimum?
pairs.derivation: Pico reports Plato asking why man is the wisest animal and answering it. Dropped the speech-tag framing 'Querens item,' before the question and 'Respondet:' with the surrounding guillemets before the answer. Question and answer are each a single verbatim clause; the next sentence (224, 'Cuius sententiae et Aristoteles meminit...') is corroboration, not part of the answer.
